# Garden Markdown contract

Garden adopts Portable Document Contract 2 as the durable document format. The normative source, parsed-envelope schema, render policy, query contract, query capability subset, and revision 2 conformance corpus are vendored here with the original MIT license. The shared corpus is pinned at `pdc-document-conformance/2`, revision 2. `packages/markdown/scripts/embed-envelope-schema.mjs` generates the package's envelope validator metadata and query parser capability table directly from these JSON contracts; `--check` detects generated drift.

The `@garden/markdown` package creates and reads canonical `pdc-document/2` Markdown, preserves source bytes during no-op access, and performs guarded metadata patches for that Markdown profile. It classifies PDC 2 HTML and legacy PDC 1 HTML/Djot as read-only source fallbacks. Its `@garden/markdown/storage` host adapter provides digest-guarded atomic replacement for an existing regular file, but does not validate content or claim Full Writer conformance. This package does not render HTML or Djot, walk a vault, resolve vault links/assets, or claim Full Reader/Writer/Mutator conformance. Plain Markdown and unmarked HTML remain visible as legacy inputs.

Queries use only the `pdc-query/1` `.base` and fenced `base` transports. `query-capabilities.json` is the machine-readable declaration of the parser's conservative portable subset; `groupBy` is recognized but remains unexecuted until the result model can represent grouped rows. The evaluator is a read-only in-memory projection. Unsupported Bases expressions, functions, keys, or views produce explicit `valid_unexecuted` diagnostics and are never evaluated as code.

The shared corpus tests exercise every `kind: file` case, including all canonical Markdown and query fixtures, readable legacy HTML and Djot classification, PDC 1 safety diagnostics, and every listed operation except metadata-patch cases on read-only profiles. The precise operation exclusions are `legacy-v1-djot-metadata-patch`, `legacy-v1-html-metadata-patch`, and `v2-html-metadata-patch`; `duplicate-document-id` is the excluded vault `set` case because this package does not index a vault. The package also does not parse HTML DOM semantics or render/sanitize HTML and Djot, or resolve assets; those remain explicit app or adapter conformance work. Atomic source replacement is available through the storage subpath and is tested separately. It does not claim full PDC 2 HTML or vault conformance.

## Editor decision

Garden provides `@garden/editor` as a library because desktop and service templates own their own shells, while several existing applications need the same source-preserving editor. A standalone Obsidian-style app is a roadmap option after the library has been used by multiple templates and its vault workflows are concrete.

The local Cassette and Oximemo implementations use `@atomic-editor/editor` 0.6.2 over CodeMirror 6. Cassette's `SourceEditor` demonstrates the safe integration seam: it composes Atomic's Markdown language, syntax, live-preview, theme, and wiki-link extensions directly, keeps the CodeMirror document string as the saved source, uses a vault-contained image resolver, and omits Atomic's table and general image widgets. Atomic's React convenience wrapper installs those table and image widgets unconditionally; Garden therefore uses the exported CodeMirror extensions instead of that wrapper. Garden now maintains a narrow local fork of Atomic inline preview so focused task lines reveal editable source; the pinned dependency and MIT attribution remain in place. Broader library distribution is deferred.

Tables and fenced code have source-preserving previews that reveal their source for editing. Standalone image, audio, Markdown and HTML embeds resolve through an explicit host callback. Unresolved references remain source; no arbitrary resource is fetched by the editor. HTML previews use an allowlist sanitizer and a restrictive sandbox. Read-only documents also use source-only mode because Atomic's task widgets can edit source. Link callbacks are supplied by the host, so document URIs are not handed to the browser by default. Labels are props supplied by the app's locale catalog.

## Presentation

[presentation.md](./presentation.md) defines shared properties, body/source presentation, query enablement, and the syntax support matrix. It complements PDC without changing its grammar.
